deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT: This page is a station adjustment of horizontal directions. It is not connected with the Gaussian-integer and biquadratic-residue work on the neighbouring pages.

The four directions are 1, 2, 5, 7. Each has an unknown correction a, b, c, d. The unit is the second of arc, and the work is carried in units of 0.001".

(A) DIRECTIONS. Two sets of provisional azimuths are written down.
- Left column: R1 = 27°44'11.535", R2 = 83°59'53.740", R5 = 200°54'24.841", R7 = 283°31'24.276".
- Right column (a revised set): R1 = 27°44'10.404", R2 = 83°59'53.449", R5 = 200°54'24.900", R7 = 283°31'25.408".

(B) OBSERVATION EQUATIONS. Six measured angles (i,k) are each given a weight p, read here as the number of repetitions. The weights are 27, 16, 16, 23, 31 and 12.
- The second column (−27, 9.7, 6.10, −23, 21.10, −12) appears to split some weights into two series: 9+7 = 16, 6+10 = 16, 21+10 = 31. This reading is my interpretation.
- The observed angles are:
  - (1,2) = 56°15'42.287"
  - (1,5) = 173°10'12.750". The value used is 12.750 (my inference from the arithmetic); it was later corrected to 14.469.
  - (2,5) = 116°54'30.250"
  - (5,7) = 82°36'58.457"
  - (7,1) = 104°12'43.435"
  - (7,2) = 160°28'28.146"
- Each equation has the form v = (R_k − R_i − observed) + (k − i), where k and i stand for the unknown corrections. For example, v12 = −0.082 − a + b.
- Left-column constants: −0.082, +0.556, +0.751, +0.978, +2.824, +1.
- Right-column constants: +0.758, +1.746, +1.201, +2.05(1), +1.561, −0.105.

(C) NORMAL EQUATIONS. Minimising Σ p v² gives the gradient vector G = g0 + N x, with
 N = [[74,−27,−16,−31],[−27,55,−16,−12],[−16,−16,55,−23],[−31,−12,−23,66]].
Every row of N sums to zero, so the system is singular: only differences of directions are determined. Each G vector therefore sums to zero, and this serves as a check.

(D) FIRST RELAXATION.
- Start: G = (−34150, −62, +97456, −63244), which sums to 0.
- Gauss changes one unknown at a time, always attacking the largest residual, in the sequence c = −1800, b = −520, d = +240, b = +50, c = −8, d = +3, b = −2.
- After each change he adds the corresponding column of N times the step. Every column on the page checks exactly.
- End residual: (−11, −10, −21, +42).
- Accumulated solution: a = 0, b = −472, c = −1808, d = +243.
- This is shifted by an arbitrary constant −121 to give (−121, −593, −1929, +122).
- The end residual is exactly the normal-equation vector of the right-column data at zero, taking l15 = 1.746. The first block's absolute terms equal those of the revised data minus N·x. So the right column is the improved set of directions (my inference).

(E) SECOND RELAXATION, on the revised data.
- The observed angle (1,5) is now corrected to 173°10'14.469", so l15 = +0.027.
- Start: G = (+27493, −10, −27526, +42).
- Steps: c = +500, a = −260, c = −75, d = +25, a = −9, c = +8, a = +2, b = +1, c = +1.
- End residual: (−11, +10, +26, −25).
- Solution: a = −267, b = +1, c = +434, d = +25.
- Adding back +121 gives the final corrections (−146, +122, +555, +146) thousandths of a second.

This is exactly the 'indirect' iterative elimination that Gauss described to Gerling (letter of 26 Dec 1823), applied to a direction set at one station.
errors: Left column, angle 2.5: R5 − R2 = 116°54'31.101", so the constant should be +0.851. The page has +0.751, a slip of 0.1". It is not propagated: the right column's +1.201 is correct.
Left column, angle 7.1: 360° + R1 − R7 = 104°12'47.259", so the constant should be +3.824. The page has +2.824, a slip of exactly 1". The right column's +1.561 is correct.
Left column, angle 7.2: the computed constant is +1.318. The page shows only '+1'; this is probably abbreviated or unfinished.
Right column, angle 5.7: the exact value is +2.051. It may be read as 2.058 in the transcription; the image is consistent with 2.051.
Second relaxation, first step, b column: −10 − 8000 = −8010. The next entry, −990 = −8010 + 7020, confirms that −8010 was used. If '−8016' is really written, it is a pen slip.
Final c residual: the page has +26, whereas the exact value is +25. This reflects ±1 rounding in the starting value of c (−27525 versus −27526); it is immaterial.

The left-column constants on the page do not themselves produce the first block's starting vector. That vector equals the revised data minus N·x, so the first block was based on a provisional set of absolute terms not fully shown on this page.

results.what: Weighted least-squares station adjustment of four directions from six repeated angle measurements. The normal equations are singular, with row sums zero.
results.modern_name: Least-squares adjustment of directions (station adjustment) via normal equations

results.what: Iterative solution of the normal equations, relaxing one unknown at a time on the largest residual, with zero-sum checks. Applied to a singular system fixed only up to an additive constant.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine geodetic worksheet showing Gauss's well-documented indirect (relaxation) method. It is the very procedure of the 1823 Gerling letter, applied to a 4-direction station. Interesting only as a further worked instance.

checkable.asserts: The normal matrix has zero row sums, i.e. it is singular.
The first relaxation ends at residual (-11,-10,-21,42).
The second relaxation ends at residual (-11,10,25,-25); the page has 26 for c owing to rounding.
The second-block starting vector (27493,-10,-27525,42) follows from the revised constants with l15 = 0.027.
The left-column 2.5 constant is 0.851, not the 0.751 written.
The left-column 7.1 constant is 3.824, not the 2.824 written.

transcription_corrections: In the a,b,c,d table, the value for c is −1808, not +1808: it is the sum of the steps c = −1800 and c = −8, and −1808 − 121 = −1929.
The crossed-out value for angle 1.5 was evidently 12.750, not 14.750, because 13.306 − 12.750 = 0.556. The superscript correction 14.469 is the value used in the second block.
The second-list constant for 5.7 is +2.051, not 2.058.
Second relaxation, c = +500 column, second entry: this is −8010, not −8016.
